analysis: Examined the two changed files. (1) docs/operations/provider-release.md: the only substantive change is the date bump (line 3) and a new sentence at lines 204-208. It says a pull-request run on a Darkbloom Sandbox that got no Darkbloom cache skips every cache step of provider-release-build and builds cold, and that release workflows never skip those steps. This is documentation only. It makes no workflow, secret, signing or registration change. Signing, notarization, R2 staging, registration, tag-gating, secret scoping (dev/staging/prod) and revocation descriptions are unchanged, so I found no regression against A-005, A-011, A-017, T-034, T-054 or TB-011. The statement that release workflows never skip cache steps is an unverified claim about .github/actions/provider-release-build/action.yml, which is not in this batch. A cold build is not a security weakening, and the sentence adds no new trust assumption. (2) libs/darkbloom-cluster/Tests/.../BoundedBufferCache.swift: a new test-only Swift Testing trait. It sets the process-wide Memory.cacheLimit to min(previous, bytes) and restores the limit and clears the cache afterward. It touches no production code, key material, network path, wire protocol or on-disk cache. The MLX freed-buffer cache is the allocator reuse pool and is unrelated to the encrypted SSD prefix cache (T-041). It references QwenTensorParallelLaunch.freedBufferCacheBytes and QwenDenseStageLoadPolicy.allocatorHeadroomBytes, which are not in the supplied evidence, so I could not confirm their signatures; a mismatch would only break the test build. Test-only global state is a reliability matter and not a security one, and the file comments say the suites are serialized. The T-028 residual-GPU-memory concern is not changed by this PR, because it affects tests only. No findings. The next pass should confirm the unseen action.yml behavior if the doc claim matters.
